summary_hint: Employer compensation statement for <employee_name> (<employer_name>): base <base_pay_current>-><base_pay_new>, bonus <bonus_actual_award>, equity <equity_award_amount> <equity_award_type>.

typed_core.name: employee_name
typed_core.why: identity — whose compensation; match to the borrower
typed_core.prompt_hint: The employee named on the statement

typed_core.name: employer_name
typed_core.why: identity — the employer issuing the statement (Deloitte, Fidelity, PayPal, ...)

typed_core.name: effective_date
typed_core.why: processor — the effective date of the new base pay / the statement's fiscal-year effective date
typed_core.prompt_hint: The 'effective' date of the new base pay (e.g. 'Effective 5/31/2026', 'effective January 01, 2026', 'Effective April 1, 2025')

typed_core.name: base_pay_current
typed_core.why: processor — the current/prior-year base pay (the stable-income anchor for IN-10/IN-11 once the earnings classifier exists)
typed_core.prompt_hint: The current base pay/salary before the increase

typed_core.name: base_pay_new
typed_core.why: processor — the new base pay after the increase
typed_core.prompt_hint: The new base pay/salary effective the effective_date

typed_core.name: base_pay_increase_amount
typed_core.why: processor — the base-pay increase amount (new minus current)

typed_core.name: bonus_target_percent
typed_core.why: processor — the bonus target/opportunity percent (of base), when stated
typed_core.prompt_hint: The 'Bonus Opportunity' / 'Bonus Target' percent; leave null if only an actual award is shown

typed_core.name: bonus_actual_award
typed_core.why: processor — the actual bonus/incentive award paid (AIP award, bonus award) — a VARIABLE-income component (the base-vs-variable split is the earnings classifier's call, not ours)

typed_core.name: equity_award_amount
typed_core.why: processor — the equity award as PRINTED. ⚠ This may be a SHARE COUNT (e.g. 625 shares) OR a DOLLAR VALUE (e.g. $50,000 RSU) depending on the employer — it is NOT normalized. Read equity_award_type to know which. NEVER sum equity_award_amount across documents (adding share counts to dollars is meaningless).
typed_core.prompt_hint: The equity award amount EXACTLY as printed — do NOT convert shares to dollars or vice versa. If shares, capture the share count; if a dollar value, capture the dollars. equity_award_type records which.

typed_core.name: equity_award_type
typed_core.why: processor — what the equity award is (RSU, Chairman's Shares, stock options, ...) — also disambiguates whether equity_award_amount is a share count or a dollar value

typed_core.name: one_time_payment_amount
typed_core.why: processor — a special/one-time discretionary payment, when stated (distinct from the recurring bonus)
typed_core.prompt_hint: A 'Special One-Time Payment' / 'Reward Excellence' / additional-award amount

typed_core.name: performance_rating
typed_core.why: processor — the year-end performance rating, when stated (context for the bonus)

rejected.name: total_compensation
rejected.reason: ⚠️ a total-comp figure (e.g. the printed '$195,000 total compensation' banner) is NOT captured. It would be read as QUALIFYING INCOME, but the base-vs-variable / usable-income call is a DECISION PROCEDURE (Priya's earnings ruling, docs/domain/priya-rulings-2026-08.md — 'do not classify solely from the text label', fail-closed UNKNOWN branch), belonging to the unbuilt earnings classifier, not the extractor. Tags describe; rules judge. It falls to the catch-all.

rejected.name: qualifying_income / usable_income
rejected.reason: a JUDGMENT — the earnings classifier's output, not a fact on the page.

rejected.name: variable_vs_base classification
rejected.reason: same — which components count as stable vs variable income is Priya's decision procedure, not an extraction label.

rejected.name: bonus_target_amount
rejected.reason: printed on only 1 of 3 samples (PayPal); derivable from base × target%. Dropped to avoid a mostly-null field (LP-461 over-recall).

rejected.name: document_date
rejected.reason: only 1 of 3 has a document date distinct from the effective date; effective_date covers the recency need.

rejected.name: employee_id
rejected.reason: an employer identifier (e.g. '00323165') — not income-relevant, and a bare digit run near the at-rest guard threshold; deliberately not captured so no _PII_FIELDS entry is needed.

rejected.name: merit / market_adjustment / bonus_funding_percent / company_performance_percent
rejected.reason: employer-SPECIFIC itemization (Deloitte's Merit/Market-Adj, Fidelity's Bonus Funding, PayPal's Company Performance %) that does not normalize across employers; the normalized components are the scalars above, the raw items fall to the catch-all (the scalars-over-list decision, A2).

encoding_variations: employers itemize very differently (Deloitte: Base Pay / AIP / Reward Excellence; Fidelity: Bonus funding / Chairman's Shares; PayPal: Bonus target / Company Performance % / RSU / one-time) — the scalars capture the NORMALIZED components, the raw items go to the catch-all
equity is a SHARE COUNT for some employers (Fidelity '625 Chairman's Shares') and a DOLLAR VALUE for others (PayPal '$50,000 RSU') — captured as printed, equity_award_type disambiguates
some statements are screenshots / phone photos of an internal portal (247 is an angled photo) — extraction confidence may be lower
the effective date appears as 'Effective <date>' for the new base pay; a fiscal-year period may also be shown

open_questions.q: Fixed scalars vs a compensation_lines[] flat-row list?
options: a compensation_lines[] list of raw items
open_questions.recommendation: SCALARS (GEET'S DECISION, LP-468): the normalized components (base/bonus/equity/one-time/rating) recur across employers with consistent MEANING and serve IN-10/IN-11's base-vs-variable split; a raw list ('Merit', 'Company Performance %') would just mirror the catch-all.

notes: Serves NO rule today (rules_served empty) — processor visibility now. It is the DIRECT input to IN-10 and IN-11 once the earnings classifier is built; recorded so the tie is explicit (ADR-362/363 standard: a type earns its place on reliable-processor-need + a concrete future rule consumer).

These three docs (Deloitte/Fidelity/PayPal) previously force-fit into commission_income_statement (a mortgage sales-commission type) and post-LP-463 divert to Tier 3 with type_matches_document=False; this type is their correct home.

No PII field and no scrub backstop: every captured scalar is a name / date / dollar amount (< 9 digits) / percent / rating / equity-type string. The one long identifier (employee_id) is deliberately not captured.
NO total/qualifying/variable-vs-base — the earnings classification is a separate, unbuilt decision procedure (Priya's ruling).
